stage1.impression: A clean, competent interior render: the plaster wall has real texture and the shade's tinted flare reads as acrylic, but the lamp does not look switched on. The wall is the brightest thing in the frame, the shade sits darker than the wall behind it, and there is no pool of light on the walnut top. The cropped, half-black loudspeaker on the left and the cabinet slivers at the bottom are clutter rather than context, and the denoiser has smoothed the wood and wall into a CG look.

blocking_9: The lit shade and its opal throat must be the brightest, most saturated element; the wall behind must sit at least a stop below the shade's glow (wall lum_median under about 120 while the shade's lit inner face holds above 130).
The lamp must visibly light its surroundings: a warm pool on the cabinet top under the shade, brighter than the top beyond it, and a shaped falloff on the wall rather than an even wash.
Dusk must read: a cool ambient from the window against the warm lamp, not a uniform pink room.
The loudspeaker must read as a whole, deliberate silhouette in the background (or be framed out), not a cropped dark slab with a crushed horn mouth at the frame edge.
No denoiser smearing on the walnut grain and plaster; no stray cabinet slivers or hot specular lines at the frame edges.
The lamp's foot needs a soft contact shadow and its own coloured spill on the walnut.

defects.what: Wall is the brightest large area (lum_median 192), brighter than the lamp's shade, so the lamp does not read as the light source.
The shade's flare body reads dull (lum_median 80) against the wall; the light through the tinted acrylic does not glow.
The opal throat insert clips (31% clipped) to a flat white-lilac blob with a hard bright crescent on its right; reads as a CG emitter.
No pool of lamp light on the cabinet top: under the shade the walnut measures lum 67, no brighter than the top beyond it (78).
Foot of the lamp has no visible contact shadow; the lower disc's pale bottom edge makes it look slightly lifted.
Loudspeaker's horn is cropped by the frame edge and its mouth is crushed to black (60% of pixels crushed in 30,280,330,600); it reads as a dark slab, not a $20,000 product.
Loudspeaker's lower body and a purple disc in the bottom-left corner are cut off and out of focus: clutter competing with the hero.
Slivers of the cabinet's drawer front with bright gaps show at the bottom edge (p95 159 against median 39).
Top-left corner falls to a muddy purple (lum 63) that does not read as any surface.
A thin hot white specular line on the shade's rim (p95 246) and another on the foot's top edge near (815, 962); look like render artefacts.
Walnut grain and the plaster are smoothed by the denoiser; micro-texture is soft and waxy.

changes.problem: The room's ambient overpowers the lamp: the wall is brighter than the lit shade, so the lamp does not read as switched on at dusk.

evidence.measured: wall lum_median 192, p95 201; shade body (620,450,780,590) lum_median 80

changes.expected: The wall far from the lamp drops by about a stop and a half and the lamp becomes the dominant light; the cool fill reads as dusk ambient in the shadows.

changes.problem: The lamp throws no pool of light on the cabinet top, so it does not light its world.

evidence.measured: walnut under the shade lum_median 67, walnut at far right (1300,920,1600,990) 78

changes.expected: A warm pool on the walnut under the shade, falling off past its rim; a brighter glow through the flare.

changes.problem: The opal throat clips to a flat white blob while the shade body stays dull.
changes.expected: The opal sleeve keeps gradation from bright core to edge, with the throat as the brightest point but not clipped.

changes.problem: The loudspeaker is cropped at the frame edge and its lower body and a disc clutter the bottom-left, while slivers of the cabinet's drawers show at the bottom.

evidence.measured: horn mouth crush_pct 60; bottom-left lum_median 34; bottom-edge slivers p95 159 vs median 39

change.to: position [1.05, -2.3, 1.05], target [0.1, 0.45, 0.85], 65 mm, f/4 (focus stays on the lamp at [0.36, 0.18, 0.98])

changes.expected: The lamp stays right-of-centre and sharp; the whole loudspeaker reads as a soft, complete silhouette behind-left; the cabinet's top edge sits clean in the lower third with no drawer slivers cut by the frame.

changes.problem: The loudspeaker's horn mouth is crushed to black, so the context product is a dark hole.
changes.expected: A warm rim and a little light inside the horn mouth so its flare reads, still well below the lamp.

changes.problem: Denoiser smoothing makes the walnut and plaster waxy, the main photographic tell.

evidence.measured: seen at 3x: grain smeared, plaster soft

change.to: 1024 (with denoiser on albedo+normal passes, or denoiser off and a 0.6 px grain added in finish)

changes.expected: Crisp walnut grain and plaster micro-texture; no blotchy low-frequency noise.

changes.problem: The foot has no contact shadow and the hot white lines on the rim and foot edge read as artefacts.

evidence.measured: rim line p95 246 against median 144; foot edge near (815,962) similar

change.to: power_w 4.0, size [1.0, 0.4] (softer, lower), so the bells' downlight sets the foot's shadow

changes.expected: A soft shadow ring around the foot, coloured spill from the discs on the walnut, no pinpoint line on the foot's edge.

changes.problem: Nothing in the frame says dusk; the room reads as an evenly lit pink box.

evidence.measured: wall top lum_median 172, evenly lit; no window or cool light visible

change.to: horizon #7F8FB8, zenith #24324F, and let the window's cool light rake across the far-left wall (set.windows along 0.9 -> 1.4 so its spill lands behind the loudspeaker)

changes.expected: A cool blue wash on the left wall behind the loudspeaker against the lamp's warm pool on the right: dusk read by colour contrast.

out_of_scope.request: The shade's tint reads darker and duller than the light passing through it would suggest.
out_of_scope.why: The shade's colour and material are fixed; addressed only through the light inside it (c2, c3).
